ApiError.description:
`{"error": {"code", "message", "type"}}`. The shared wire DTO; the
daemon-side `ApiErrorCode` enum is the source of truth for which
`code`, `message`, and `type` go together.

error.description: The nested body with the actual error metadata.

code.description:
Short slug identifying the error class. Clients may switch on
these strings; the [`ApiErrorCodeSlug`] enum enumerates every
value the daemon emits.

type.description:
OpenAI's taxonomy — [`ApiErrorKind::InvalidRequestError`] for
things the client could have avoided, [`ApiErrorKind::ServerError`]
for daemon-side problems. Derived from the daemon's `ApiErrorCode`
variant.

ApiErrorCodeSlug.description:
Stable wire slug identifying an error class. Clients may switch on
these strings. The `Other` variant is a deserialization fallback so
clients don't break when the daemon adds a new code before they're
updated.

Variant names are serialised as `snake_case` strings (e.g.
`ModelNotFound` → `"model_not_found"`) via `#[serde(rename_all)]`.
The one exception is [`ApiErrorCodeSlug::InvalidRequest`], which
serialises as `"invalid_request_error"` to match OpenAI's
error-type taxonomy.

ApiErrorKind.description:
OpenAI's error-type taxonomy. `InvalidRequestError` for anything the
client could have avoided, `ServerError` for daemon-side problems.
`Other` is a deserialization fallback.

ChatCompletionChunk.description:
One `data:` chunk of a streamed completion, or a whole non-streamed
response body.

choices.description: Absent on chunks that carry only `usage`.

oneOf.description: llama.cpp's non-standard per-request timing block.
Token counts, when the engine reported them.

model.description: Model name (maps to an ananke service name).

ChatCompletionEnvelope.description:
`POST /v1/chat/completions` request envelope.

The daemon only interprets the `model` field; all other keys are
forwarded verbatim to the upstream service.

Choice.description:
One completion candidate. Streaming responses fill `delta`,
non-streaming ones fill `message`.

oneOf.description: Set on a streamed chunk.
Set on a non-streamed body.

model.description: Model name (maps to an ananke service name).

CompletionEnvelope.description:
`POST /v1/completions` request envelope.

The daemon only interprets the `model` field; all other keys are
forwarded verbatim to the upstream service.

hash.description: SHA-256 of `content`, base64-encoded; used as an `If-Match` value on PUT.

writable.description:
Whether the config file can be written to. `false` when the file
is on a read-only store (e.g. NixOS-managed); the frontend should
start the editor in read-only mode.

content.description: Raw TOML to validate without persisting.

ContainerDetail.description: Container identity for a service running under Docker/Podman.

container_id.description: Live container ID, present only while a container is running.

container_name.description: Live container name, present only while a container is running.

config_path.description: Path of the active configuration file.

uptime_ms.description: Milliseconds since this daemon instance started.

DashboardEvents.description: Retained events and the actual beginning of this daemon's capture window.

events.description: Events in publication order; the bounded history survives browser reconnects.

since_ms.description: Oldest retained event time, or the daemon's capture start when empty.

oneOf.description: A read result, pushed snapshot, or mutation acknowledgement.

body.description: The endpoint's generated response DTO, or null for an empty response.

oneOf.description: A fragment of the existing OpenAI event stream.

text.description: UTF-8 SSE data, preserving upstream frame boundaries across fragments.

oneOf.description: The stream has ended; absence of an OpenAI DONE marker remains an error.

DashboardMessage.description: A response or pushed snapshot; JSON bodies use the existing endpoint schemas.

oneOf.description: The service inventory.
One service's current state and placement.
The latest hardware measurements.
Daemon addresses, configuration path, and uptime.
OpenAI-compatible model discovery.
Retained lifecycle events from this daemon instance.
Persisted request metrics.
Persisted automatic restart records.
Persisted device measurements.
A page of captured child-process logs.

before.description: An opaque cursor for older lines.

oneOf.description: The configuration file and its concurrency hash.

DashboardQuery.description: A dashboard read; subscriptions receive an initial snapshot and subsequent updates.

DashboardRange.description: A historical window, optionally following the server clock.

live_ms.description: A rolling window's duration; fixed windows omit this field.

since.description: Inclusive lower bound for a fixed window, in Unix milliseconds.

until.description: Inclusive upper bound for a fixed window, in Unix milliseconds.

oneOf.description: Read once or subscribe until cancelled.
Cancel a subscription or an in-progress request.
Execute a service lifecycle command.
Validate a configuration draft.
Save a draft using the same optimistic concurrency contract as HTTP.

hash.description: The hash returned by the last configuration read.

oneOf.description: Stream a chat completion until completion or cancellation.

DashboardRequest.description: One client operation, correlated by its request or subscription id.

DeviceFootprint.description: One device's share of a [`ServiceSummary`]'s footprint.

bytes.description: Memory bytes the service would occupy on that device.

device.description: Slot string: `"cpu"` or `"gpu:N"`, as the placement engine names it.

DevicePlacement.description:
One device's share of a [`PlacementPreview`], with enough context to draw a
utilisation bar: this service's share, what is already in use by everything
else, and the device's total capacity.

bytes.description:
Memory bytes this service reserves on the device — the pledge floor for a
dynamic service.

max_bytes.description:
Upper bound this service could grow to on the device. Equals `bytes`
for fixed-size services; larger for a dynamic command service that may
borrow up to its configured maximum.

total_bytes.description: Total memory capacity of the device, in bytes. Zero if unknown.

used_by_others_bytes.description:
Memory bytes already in use on the device by everything except this
service (for a running service, its own resident memory is excluded so
`used_by_others_bytes + bytes` doesn't double-count it).

DeviceReservation.description: One reservation held against a device.

elastic.description: Whether the reservation is elastic (dynamic service borrowing).

DeviceShortfall.description:
One device's contribution to a placement failure.

The binding constraint is often host RAM rather than GPU VRAM — a MoE with
expert offload routinely spills the bulk of its weights to the CPU — so the
device is named rather than the failure being sorted into a category.

device.description:
Device id string, e.g. `"gpu:0"` or `"cpu"`. Matches `DeviceSummary::id`
from `GET /api/devices`, so a shortfall can be cross-referenced against
the live device view.

requested_bytes.description: Bytes the placement needed on this device.

DisableResponse.description:
`POST /api/services/{name}/disable` response body.

The `status` tag tells the caller the outcome of the disable request. All
variants are success states; a request that fails validation or targets a
missing service comes back as an error response instead.

model.description: Model name (maps to an ananke service name).

EmbeddingEnvelope.description:
`POST /v1/embeddings` request envelope.

The daemon only interprets the `model` field; all other keys are
forwarded verbatim to the upstream service.

EnableResponse.description:
`POST /api/services/{name}/enable` response body.

The `status` tag tells the caller the outcome of the enable request.

EnvVar.description: One environment variable ananke sets on the child process.

EstimateSummary.description:
Estimator output projected to the wire. Carries the components a
reader needs to answer "how much memory will this service take?"
without having to re-derive any of them client-side.

compute_buffer_bytes_per_device.description: Compute-buffer reservation per active device, in bytes.

configured_context.description: Configured context window the estimate is sized against.

kv_bytes_for_context.description:
`kv_per_token × configured_context`. Precomputed so the
frontend can render the total directly.

kv_per_token.description:
KV cache bytes per context token. Zero for SSM/Mamba
architectures with no KV cache.

weights_bytes.description: Static weight bytes (including mmproj if configured).

oneOf.description: A service's state machine moved to a new state.

at_ms.description: When the transition happened, in unix milliseconds.

from.description: The state it left, e.g. `"starting"` or `"running"`.

oneOf.description:
A service's reservation table changed (a pledge was added, moved, or
released on one or more devices).

at_ms.description: When the allocation changed, in unix milliseconds.

reservations.description:
The per-device reserved byte counts after the change. Keys are
device ids (`"cpu"` or `"gpu:N"`).

oneOf.description: The config was reloaded or replaced, and a set of services changed.

at_ms.description: When the reload happened, in unix milliseconds.

changed_services.description: The services whose effective config changed as a result.

oneOf.description:
One of a service's rolling estimator corrections moved by more than 5%.
`class` is the memory pool it belongs to — `"vram"` or `"host"` — since
the two are learned independently from separate observations.

at_ms.description: When the drift was recorded, in unix milliseconds.

oneOf.description:
A `Running` service was drained and respawned by its auto-restart
policy. `trigger` is `"error_rate"`, `"periodic"`, `"ttft_stall"`,
`"generation_stall"`, or `"spec_collapse"`; `detail` is a
human-readable reason (e.g. the observed error rate and window).

at_ms.description: When the restart was recorded, in unix milliseconds.

detail.description: A human-readable reason for the restart.

oneOf.description:
The event bus dropped events because a subscriber fell behind. The
event carries no `at_ms` — it is generated by the bus itself.

dropped.description: How many events were dropped for the slow subscriber.

Event.description:
One event delivered over `/api/events`. The `type` tag discriminates the
variant; `at_ms` is present on every variant except `overflow`. The same
`Event` is used as a broadcast bus message internally, so it must stay
serializable and stable — anything published here is part of the wire
contract the frontend and other clients read.

oneOf.description: Starts now in currently-free memory — no eviction needed.

Fits within the hardware, but currently-free memory is insufficient, so
the daemon would reclaim or evict lower-priority peers to make room.

No placement is possible under current conditions, even with every other
service gone. `shortfalls` names the devices that came up short and by
how much. Empty when there is no device to point at: a configuration
error that no amount of freed memory would fix, or a host with no
eligible device for this service at all.

shortfalls.description: The devices that came up short, and by how much.

FitVerdict.description:
Whether a service's estimated placement fits under current conditions.

Serialised as a `kind`-tagged union so a failing verdict can carry the
per-device numbers that explain it.

IkParams.description:
The ik_llama.cpp knobs of a `runtime = { kind = "ik-llama", ... }`
service, mirrored from the validated config.

attn_max_batch.description: `-amb` attention scratch cap in MiB, when set.

LaunchCommand.description:
One launch command — argv and environment. Discriminated by the
optional `container` block: when `None` this is a native process (the
existing shape, byte-identical for process consumers); when `Some` it is
a containerized workload carrying the runtime create command plus the
in-container argv.

argv.description:
The argv. For a native process `argv[0]` is the binary and the rest
are its arguments. For a container this is the *in-container* argv,
which for a `llama-cpp` service is flags only — the executable is
the image's own entrypoint and does not appear here. Already split
into tokens; no shell quoting is applied, so a client rendering a
copy-pasteable line should quote as needed.

oneOf.description:
Container launch details when this is a containerized workload.
`None` (and thus absent from JSON) for a native process.

env.description:
Environment variables ananke sets or overrides for the child (notably
`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`), sorted by key. Not the full inherited
environment.

env_inherit.description:
Whether the child process also inherits the daemon's full
environment (`$PATH`, `$HOME`, locale, …) on top of `env`. When
`false`, the child sees only the variables in `env`.

source.description:
Whether the service is running (`running`) or this is a preview of the
next start (`preview`).

LaunchCommandResponse.description:
Response from `GET /api/services/{name}/command`: the launch command
computed under two scenarios.

oneOf.description:
Command against the current device state and pledge book. `None`
when the service can't fit alongside currently running services.

on_empty.description:
Command on an empty cluster — what the service would launch with
if no other services held pledges. Always present when the service
can fit on the hardware at all.

LaunchCommandSource.description: Whether a [`LaunchCommand`] describes a live process or a what-if.

LaunchContainer.description:
Container-specific half of a launch preview. Present only when the
service carries a `[service.container]` block.

argv.description: In-container argv (the command that runs inside the container).

create_argv.description: The exact, shell-free `create` argv ananke will invoke.

env.description: Explicit environment keys and values set inside the container.

env_passthrough.description:
Environment variable names passed through from the host, without
resolving their (possibly secret) values.

gpu_devices.description: Expanded CDI GPU device entries (one per allocated GPU).

name_pattern.description:
Generated name pattern (`ananke-<service>-<run-id>`; the run id is a
runtime value and not expanded in a preview).

publication.description:
Service port publication (`host_ip:host_port:container_port`) for
bridge networking, or `None` for host networking.

LaunchMount.description: A bind mount in a container launch preview.

seq.description: Sequence number within `(service_id, run_id)`, monotonic per run.

timestamp_ms.description: Millisecond UNIX timestamp the line was received.

oneOf.description: One captured log line.
Subscriber lagged; this many frames were dropped.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for paging further back; `None` when exhausted.

MessageBody.description: The text of a choice, whether incremental or complete.

content.description:
The answer text itself. `None` when the engine sent structured
content parts rather than a plain string — ananke has no use for
those, and reading them is not worth failing the chunk over.

reasoning.description: Reasoning text under the plainer key some engines use instead.

MetricBucketResponse.description: One time bucket of aggregated request metrics, scoped to a single service.

avg_duration_ms.description: Average request duration in milliseconds, if any requests had timing data.

avg_ttft_ms.description: Average time-to-first-token in milliseconds (streaming requests only).

bucket_start.description: Start of the bucket (ms since epoch).

completion_tokens.description: Total completion tokens across all requests in the bucket.

effective_tps.description:
End-to-end effective generation throughput: completion tokens divided
by total wall-clock duration, so prefill, TTFT, and queue wait all
count against it. Available whenever the bucket has any request with a
recorded duration, including non-streaming requests with no engine
timings where no decode window exists to derive `output_tps`. Always
≤ `output_tps`; the UI surfaces it as the fallback line and as the
end-to-end figure. A bucket that generated no tokens (e.g. only
embeddings or stalled requests) is `null`, not zero.

error_count.description: Number of requests with a 4xx/5xx status code.

input_tps.description:
Input tokens per second during prompt processing: prompt tokens
divided by total TTFT. `None` if no timed requests in the bucket.

output_tps.description:
Output tokens per second during decode: completion tokens divided by
total decode time. `None` if no timed requests in the bucket.

prompt_tokens.description: Total prompt tokens across all requests in the bucket.

request_count.description: Number of requests in the bucket.

service.description:
Service name these metrics belong to. `None` if the service has been
deleted from the database but metric rows remain.

Modality.description:
What kind of model the service exposes through the OpenAI-compatible
API. Drives badge rendering in the frontend and lets clients (Discord
rotation, RAG indexers) filter the model list by purpose without
parsing `metadata.*` strings.

Defaults to `Chat`, and the field is elided from the wire when it is,
so a chat service carries no `modality` key in its config or payloads.

ModelInfo.description:
GGUF-derived facts about a model file. Read once per service per
daemon run and cached; the file isn't re-parsed on every detail
poll.

block_count.description:
Layer count exposed by the architecture's `{arch}.block_count`
metadata key, when present.

file_name.description:
File name (basename of shard 0). Useful for the UI to show the
underlying filename without the full path.

has_mmproj.description:
`true` when the service has a configured `mmproj` GGUF — the
standard signal for vision / multimodal support.

license.description:
`general.license` if declared (`"apache-2.0"`, `"llama3.3"`,
`"gemma"`, …). Surfaced so operators can see the licence
without leaving the dashboard.

model_name.description:
Friendly name declared in `general.name`, when the publisher
set one. Typically the upstream model identifier ("Qwen3 32B",
"Llama 3.3 70B Instruct", …) rather than ananke's service
name. Absent for hand-built GGUFs that left the field blank.

parameter_count.description:
`general.parameter_count` if declared by the publisher. Modern
converter tools (Unsloth, bartowski's repacks, …) write this;
older GGUFs may not. The field is the model's *parameter*
count, not the on-disk byte size — quantisation makes the two
diverge by a large factor.

shard_count.description: Number of shards discovered. 1 for a single-file GGUF.

total_tensor_bytes.description:
Sum of every tensor's byte size across every shard. The
reference number when sizing the model on disk.

trained_context_length.description:
The model's *trained* context window, read from
`{arch}.context_length`. The service's configured context may
be lower.

ananke_metadata.description:
Passthrough entries from `[[service]] metadata.*`. Non-standard
OpenAI field, elided when empty; strict OpenAI clients ignore it.

modality.description:
What kind of OpenAI endpoint this model serves. Non-standard
OpenAI field, elided when [`Modality::Chat`] (the default), so
strict OpenAI clients never see it; embedding clients can filter
on it.

PlacementPreview.description:
Where a service's memory would land per device under current conditions, and
whether it fits without the daemon having to evict or reclaim. Computed by
running the placement engine against the live snapshot and pledge book.

devices.description:
Per-device memory the service would occupy, sorted by device. Keys are
slot strings (`"cpu"`, `"gpu:0"`, …); values are bytes.

expert_offload_bytes.description:
Total expert-tensor bytes the packer offloaded to the CPU for a MoE
model (auto/manual `expert_offload`). Zero for non-MoE services or when
nothing was offloaded.

expert_offload_layers.description: Number of distinct layers with at least one expert offloaded to the CPU.

verdict.description: Whether the placement fits right now without eviction or reclaim.

at_ms.description: Wall-clock timestamp of the firing (ms since epoch).

detail.description: Human-readable reason (e.g. the observed error rate and window).

run_id.description: The run that was drained by the firing.

restarts.description: Firings within the requested window, oldest first.

RuntimeInfo.description:
Which llama-server implementation serves a llama-cpp service, plus
the fork-specific configuration when it is not mainline.

oneOf.description: ik_llama.cpp parameters; present only when `kind == "ik-llama"`.

Container identity for a containerized service. `None` for native
host processes. Kept beside the llama-cpp `runtime`/`serving` cards
so containerized llama.cpp retains its engine semantics.

current_allocation.description:
What pledge the service is currently holding on each device.
Empty when idle. Keys are slot strings (`"cpu"`, `"gpu:0"`, …),
values are MiB.

oneOf.description:
Memory estimate computed against the service's configured context
and KV cache settings. Same caching rules as `model_info`.

last_used_ms.description:
Wall-clock timestamp (ms since epoch) of the last time the
service was provisioned or received a request. `None` if the
service has never been started.

modality.description:
What kind of OpenAI endpoint the service serves. See
[`crate::services::list::ServiceSummary::modality`] for the rendering rule.

oneOf.description:
GGUF-derived facts about the model file. `None` for command-
template services and for llama-cpp services whose GGUF couldn't
be read (file missing, unrecognised, etc.). Cached in the daemon
after the first successful read so repeated detail polls don't
re-parse the file.

observed_peak_bytes.description: Observed memory peak (VRAM + RSS) across the service's lifetime.

placement_override.description: Manual placement override, keyed by device slot string.

oneOf.description:
Per-device placement the service would take under current conditions,
plus whether it fits without eviction. `None` for command-template
services, services with a manual `placement_override`, and llama-cpp
services whose GGUF couldn't be read.

recent_logs.description: Most recent log lines for a frontend's first-paint context.

recent_restarts.description:
Recent auto-restart watchdog firings, most recent first. Sourced
from the daemon's durable `service_restarts` store, so firings are
visible after the fact — not only to a live `/api/events` listener.

rolling_mean.description:
Rolling estimator correction factor for the service's VRAM footprint.
`None` until the first observation lands.

rolling_mean_host.description:
Rolling estimator correction factor for the service's host-RAM
footprint, learned independently of the VRAM one. `None` for a service
that holds nothing in host RAM, which never accumulates a sample.

oneOf.description:
Serving-runtime details for a llama-cpp service. `None` for
command-template services.

Curated serving knobs for a llama-cpp service. `None` for
command-template services.

ServiceRestartEntry.description:
One auto-restart watchdog firing, with the service it belongs to.
The service-detail endpoint serves the same records scoped to one
service; this shape adds the `service` label for cross-service views.

at_ms.description: Wall-clock timestamp of the firing (ms since epoch).

detail.description: Human-readable reason carried by the event.

run_id.description: The run that was drained by the firing.

ananke_metadata.description:
Passthrough entries from `[[service]] metadata.*`. Empty when
none are set, and the field is elided from JSON when the map is
empty, so the key appears only for a service that opts in to
metadata.

oneOf.description:
Whether the service's estimated placement fits under current
device conditions. `None` when the verdict can't be computed
(e.g. a llama-cpp service whose GGUF hasn't been read yet).
Running services are always `Fits`.

footprint_bytes.description:
Total bytes the service would occupy across all devices — GPU VRAM and
host RAM alike — under current conditions. Includes weights, KV cache,
and compute buffer.

Normally this is the placement preview's per-device sum: what the
service would actually reserve. When `fit_verdict` is `does_not_fit`
there is no placement to sum, so this falls back to the estimator's
aggregate demand — how much the model *would need*. Read the two fields
together; a `does_not_fit` verdict means this figure is a requirement,
not a reservation.

`None` when neither can be computed (e.g. a command service that
reserves nothing, or a llama-cpp service whose GGUF hasn't been read).

footprint_devices.description:
Where [`Self::footprint_bytes`] would land, per device, sorted by device.

The same figure broken out rather than a second one: the total is this
list's sum, so a row can show both without the two disagreeing. Empty when
there is no placement to describe, which is the same condition that leaves
`footprint_bytes` `None`.

Deliberately slimmer than the detail view's `DevicePlacement`, which also
carries each device's capacity and what else is using it. Those support a
utilisation bar; a list row only names where the memory goes, and this
endpoint is polled every two seconds.

has_mmproj.description:
`true` when the service's `[[service.llama_cpp]]` config has a
`mmproj` entry — the standard signal that it supports vision /
multimodal input. `None` for non-llama-cpp services. Cheap
enough (config-only check) to ship on every list entry.

inflight_count.description:
Number of requests currently in flight through the proxy for this
service. Zero when the service is not running.

last_used_ms.description:
Wall-clock timestamp (ms since epoch) of the last time the
service was provisioned or received a request. `None` if the
service has never been started.

modality.description:
What kind of OpenAI endpoint the service serves. Elided from
JSON when [`Modality::Chat`] (the default), so a chat service's
row carries no `modality` key; embedding services explicitly
declare `modality = "embedding"` in their `[[service]]` block.

openai_compat.description: Whether the service supports the OpenAI multiplexer.

port.description: Public port the proxy listens on.

run_id.description: Active run id if currently running.

web_ui_url.description: Published service UI URL from `metadata.web_ui_url`, when configured.

openai_api_port.description: Port the OpenAI-compatible API is listening on.

ServingConfig.description:
Curated serving configuration for a llama-cpp service: the knobs an
operator reaches for when comparing services or debugging
performance, plus derived values (per-slot context) that no single
config key or argv flag states directly.

binary.description:
The llama-server executable path serving this service. With
multiple runtimes installed (mainline + ik_llama), which binary
a service uses is a first-class fact.

cache_type_k.description: KV cache type for keys (`f16` when unset).

cache_type_v.description: KV cache type for values (`f16` when unset).

draft_model.description:
Draft model file name (not full path), when a separate draft
GGUF is configured.

effective_context_per_slot.description:
The context window a single request actually gets: `context`
divided by `parallel` when the KV pool is statically split,
or the full window when unified (slots borrow from each other).

expert_offload.description: MoE expert-offload mode: `"off"`, `"auto"`, or a layer count.

spec_type.description: `--spec-type` value, when speculative decoding is on.

oneOf.description: The service was already running when the start request arrived.
The service entered `Starting` and this spawning run's id.

run_id.description: The id of the run that was spawned.

oneOf.description:
The start was queued instead of run: the service has a
`start_queue_depth` cap and the queue was full.

The supervisor declined to start: it didn't fit, the service
is disabled, etc. The embedded [`ApiErrorBody`] carries the
same typed slug, message, and kind that a 503 `ApiError`
response would (so clients can switch on `error.code` instead
of pattern-matching a freeform `reason` string). The 202 status
is preserved because this is a "controlled outcome" of the
start request, not a server-side fault.

error.description:
The typed error the supervisor produced, matching what a 503
`ApiError` response would carry.

StartResponse.description:
`POST /api/services/{name}/start` response body.

The `status` tag tells the caller the outcome of the start request.

StopResponse.description:
`POST /api/services/{name}/stop` response body.

The `status` tag tells the caller the outcome of the stop request.

Timings.description:
llama.cpp's engine-reported phase timings, which sit next to `usage`.
Absent for engines that do not emit them.

draft_n.description:
Speculative draft tokens proposed. Present only when the engine
ran speculative decoding.

prompt_n.description:
Prompt tokens actually evaluated — cache hits excluded, which is
what makes this the right prefill-throughput numerator rather
than `usage.prompt_tokens`.

Usage.description:
Token counts. Emitted in the final chunk of a stream when the client
asked for `stream_options.include_usage`, and always on a
non-streamed body.

prompt_tokens.description: Prompt tokens billed, cached prefix included.

ValidationError.description: One validation error from the config parser.

column.description: 1-based column number in the TOML source.

line.description: 1-based line number in the TOML source.
